[h1][b] TLDR: A good roguelike for a game in 2013. The mechanics can be a bit dated, and no ability to save in a run is a big negative. [/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Tons of power-ups
➕Music
➕Enemy variety

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Can’t aim/can only shoot horizontally
➖No save feature(?!)
➖Massively dependent on RNG - both in level setup(!) and items

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world here consists of various biomes that appear to be mostly randomly generated. It reminds me a lot of Dead Cells how they are random, but certain parts are always the same - as a collectable in the bottom right or something. Since each level is on a 2D platforming plane, there isn’t much depth to exploration. In fact, with how the mechanics work, you should try to speed through the levels as fast as you can. Really the only thing that you’ll be on the lookout for within the world are chests to get stronger, but that’s really it. I found the worlds to be only okay, nothing really noteworthy. 

The narrative is very simple, you crash-landed on a planet after your ship was attacked and you have to leave. That’s about it. This is told through the opening cutscene when starting up the game, so there is not a focus in-game for any sort of narrative. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
The mechanics are very similar to other roguelike games - you traverse through randomly generated levels, get random items to power up your character to hopefully keep going and beat the big bad boss. I found the mechanics to be good, if a bit simplistic. 
The idea is rushing through the levels as fast as you can because the longer you take, the harder the game gets. But you also need to balance exploration in order to find items to make yourself more powerful. I found RNG to be a big issue with how the “Rushing” style works. You need to find a specific place on the map to progress to the next level, but levels can be quite intricate, often consisting of many floors, both upwards and downwards, making it very easy to get lost and spend excessive time trying to find the exit. Combined with finding the random placement of items, which are random, it's RNG upon RNG which often leads to a very quick defeat with the occasional long win. 
I’ve won a few times with each winning run taking over 40 minutes, and throughout this, you cannot leave the game. There is no ability to save mid run. This is by far my biggest negative. 

The difficulty is mostly fair, but can definitely approach the area of hard. You can get massacred very quickly if you get in a bad spot, or if you don’t get good items, or if you simply can’t locate the teleporter. There are a lot of elements that work against you, and each minute of exploration amplifies the failure rate if you have nothing to show for it. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Technical) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
Very simple pixel-style. I would say this is probably Playstation 2-era. Despite the simplicity, the pixels themselves are crisp. 

On the technical side, I noticed no bugs or issues. 
I played using both KBM and controller, in the end I preferred controller due to platforming. I would have went with KBM if you could actually aim, but you cannot and it's mostly horizontal only. 
i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | Windows 11 installed on SSD 

[h1] [b] Audio – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
I found the music to be fairly good. It’s pretty unique and picks up during times of intensity, like when you activate a teleporter. 

There is no voice acting that I noticed. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
True to most roguelikes, I think there is some good replay value for unlockables and achievements. In my 8h of playtime, I have about a 30% completion, winning 3x and that was enough for me to give my thoughts. Aside from unlockables and achievements, there is coop gameplay, but I believe you need to have a friend to play, I don’t think there are online lobbies. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
Risk of Rain Returns (RoRR) is a true rogueLIKE experience, not lite. There are no stats or upgrades that carry over between runs, other than the item unlockables you get from completing a goal. Due to this, the difficulty can be rather intense at times and be very reliant on RNG, both from items and the way the levels work. 

I felt that RoRR is a solid roguelike experience, but I would consider it a product of its time. The base game released in 2013, and Returns came out 10 years later as a type of enhanced edition. But the gameplay, controls, and mechanics are still a product of the 2013-era of games. And I think it does hold up good, but when you have other 2D roguelikes like Dead Cells ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/588650?snr=1_5_9__402]review here[/url]) improving the formula in every way, it makes RoRR a hard sell, especially with Risk of Rain 2 out. 

What exactly is holding RoRR back for me? I would say it is two things - lack of saving and the horizontal aiming. 
The lack of saving is, in my opinion, terrible in a roguelike game. I want to be able to save at almost any time possible to make playing on things like the Steam Deck a valid choice. As it stands now, you have no option to. So when you sit down, you have to be prepared to spend either ~5 or ~45 minutes on a run, depending on how it goes. This kills the Deck option for me, as sometimes I can’t dedicate a full time to a run of a game on the go. 
As for the horizontal aiming, this is the prime example of what I mean when I call RoR a “Product of its time”. Horizontal aiming feels so limited, and you’re almost forced into using the classes that can get around the aim restriction (Pilot and Engineer, somewhat). 

So overall, yes, I would recommend RoRR, but just know that there are better options out there, like RoR2 (presumably, I haven’t played it yet, but it looks very good), or Dead Cells if you want to remain in the 2D space. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]Yes[/h1]
Base price of $15 is fair, and sale price of around $9 is obviously better. I would recommend it on sale only, otherwise, check out Dead Cells.
